# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. PLACEMENT & MARKING GAMES

### A. Light/Vision-Based
- **Akari** - Place light bulbs with illumination rules
- **Kurotto** - Place black cells with continuous extension rules

### B. Number Placement
- **Sudoku** - Fill grid with 1-9 in rows/columns/blocks
- **Nansuke** - Fill grid with numbered list entries
- **Fillomino** - Fill blocks with numbers matching block size
- **Ripple Effect** - Fill rooms with consecutive numbers
- **Makaro** - Fill rooms with directional number constraints

### C. Shape/Block Placement
- **Shikaku** - Divide grid into numbered rectangles
- **Hebi** - Place sequential snake numbers (1-5)
- **Evolomino** - Place evolving polyominoes along arrows
- **Pencils** - Mark pencils and draw lines from tips

### D. Circle/Object Movement
- **Satogaeri** - Move circles to occupy countries
- **Yosenabe** - Move circles into gray areas with sum constraints

## II. COLORING & SHADING GAMES

### A. Binary Coloring (Black/White)
- **Hitori** - Color cells to eliminate duplicates
- **Kurodoko** - Color black cells with visibility constraints
- **Nurikabe** - Color black cells forming continuous wall
- **Usowan** - Color cells with neighbor number constraints (one wrong per region)
- **Tilepaint** - Color tiles by diagonal number constraints
- **Sto-stone** - Color cells that "drop" to fill bottom half

### B. Multi-Cell Coloring
- **Heyawake** - Paint cells in rooms with constraints
- **Nurimeizu** - Paint cells to create maze from S to G
- **Nurimisaki** - Paint cells around "Misaki" promontories
- **Norinori** - Color two blocks per region
- **Nuritwin** - Shade two equal-sized blocks per region
- **LITS** - Color four-cell tetrominoes per region

### C. Triangle/Diamond Coloring
- **Shakashaka** - Place black triangles forming rectangles/squares

## III. LINE & LOOP DRAWING GAMES

### A. Single Loop Games
- **Slitherlink** - Connect dots with lines forming loop
- **Masyu** - Draw loop through circles with bend rules
- **Dotchi-Loop** - Draw loop through white circles with turn constraints
- **Nagareru** - Draw directional loop through arrow cells
- **Moon-or-Sun** - Draw loop alternating moon/sun through rooms
- **Yajilin** - Draw loop avoiding numbered black cells
- **Suraromu** - Draw loop starting/ending at numbered circle, passing gates
- **Mid-loop** - Draw loop with black circles as midpoints

### B. Path Connection Games
- **Numberlink** - Connect paired numbers with non-crossing lines
- **Hashiwokakero** - Connect islands with bridges (max 2 per pair)

## IV. REGION & BLOCK DIVISION GAMES

### A. Shaped Block Division
- **Sashigane** - Divide into L-shaped blocks with knee markers
- **Chained Block** - Fill black blocks that chain together
- **Choco Banana** - Color rectangles/squares (black/white binary)
- **Double Choco** - Divide into blocks with paired white/gray mirror shapes
- **Five Cells** - Divide into exactly 5-cell blocks with boundary numbers

### B. Free Division
- **Shikaku** - Divide into rectangles with number constraints

## V. DIRECTION & MOVEMENT GAMES

### A. Arrow/Direction-Based
- **Juosan** - Fill cells with directional marks (— or |) in territories
- **Evolomino** - Evolve shapes along directional arrows

## VI. HYBRID GAMES

- **Nurimeizu** - Combines coloring (maze creation) with path requirements
- **Sto-stone** - Combines coloring with gravity/spatial mechanics

---

**Note:** Games are categorized by their primary solving mechanic. Some games involve multiple mechanics but are placed in their dominant category.
